caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1205 of 2003
lawyer:
AJ Mohammad Ali, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mvi. Md Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner. 
Abdur Razzaq, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent No.1. 
Not Represented ------ Respondent Nos. 2-6.
parties:
Smart Apparels (Pvt.) Ltd ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Hanvit Bank Kuni Bong Branch and ors  ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Fazlul Karim J: The plaintiff-petitioner seeks leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 27-7-2003 passed by the High Court Division in First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 234 of 2003 allowing the appeal arising out of order No.2 dated 14-2-2000 passed in Title Suit No.32 of 2000 by the learned Joint District Judge, Court No.1, Dhaka restraining defendant Nos.1-4 (respondent Nos.3-4 herein) from making the payment to the corresponding Bank under letters of credit being Nos. BBA/01/99/565/DP and BBA/01/99/564/DP both dated 20-10-1999 and restraining defendant No.5 (respondent No.2 herein) from making any payment under the said letters of credit thereby allowing appeal. 

 2. The plaintiff-petitioner filed the suit for permanent injunction stating, inter alia, that AM Apparels Co. Ltd. RM 201 2nd HAW- Tan Building 112 POI Dong Kangnam Ku, Seoul, Korea wanted to purchase 22,094 pes of Men's Wind Breaker Jacket from the plaintiff for which the above firm opened letter of credit (LC) in favour of the defendant No.1 which is a buying house and placed the order with the plaintiff for manufacturing and export of above mentioned Men's Wind Breaker Jacket to Korea and transferred the aforesaid letter of credit in favour of the plaintiff. The defendant No.1 is the first beneficiary of the LC which they obtained from their principal the above AM Apparels Co. Ltd. Seoul, Korea. On receipt of the order and the LC being No. M04U1909SN00210 dated 28th September, 1999 for US$ 349971,15 from defendant No. 1 on transfer of the same in favour and to the plaintiff along. with order to manufacture 22.094 pes Men's Wind Breaker Jacket the plaintiff kept the aforesaid LC under lien to and with Sonali Bank, Bangabandhu Avenue Corporate Branch. defendant No.5 for further transaction including opening of back to back Letter of Credit for import of fabrics and accessories and export the above mentioned garments. The defendant No.1 nominated the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 and advised the plaintiff for opening LC in favour of the defendant Nos.2 and 3 respectively for import of fabrics accessories for them. Accordingly, the plaintiff opened back to back UC. No. BBA/ 01/99/565/DP dated 12-10-1999 for US$ 1,30,720.48 in favour of defendant No.2 and back to back LC being No. BBA/01/99/564/DP dated 12- 10- 1999 for US$ 1,49,252 in favour of defendant No.3. Against the aforesaid LCs, the nominated suppliers of defendant No.1 supplied/exported the fabrics and accessories and on receipt of which the plaintiff started production of the garments as stated above for export and supply to defendant No.1 and through it to its principal .The production of the said garments was under the close supervision of the defendant No.1 and were manufactured maintaining high quality as per order of the buyer. The production of the entire consignment i.e. 22,094 pcs, was completed by 4th January, 2000 which was ahead of before shipment date. That on completion of the production the plaintiff requested the buyer to complete the final inspection of the garments for shipment. On several requests of the plaintiff for the same, the defendant No.1 as the local agent of the buyer and the buying house visited the plaintiffs factory for inspection of the manufactured garments. It came with a company named Ms Hana Reports for inspection who was although not the designated/ nominated inspecting firm in terms of the LC but yet the plaintiff allowed the inspection by them due to insistence of defendant No.1 for and on behalf of its principal, the buyer. It was also allowed on the consideration that Eid-ul-Fitr holiday was nearing and the shipment date also coming closer. It was also considered by the plaintiff that if the inspection was refused the shipment date will expire without shipment of the sold out manufactured garments. After the aforesaid inspection, a report was given indicating that the manufactured garments were good and the same were found as per required quality and standard and the said inspecting organisation conducted second and final inspection on 20th January, 1999 and found the garments good and fit to be exported. The defendant No.1, at this stage, informed that they will soon give necessary instruction for shipment of the goods/garments. Thereafter, a person came from Korea and conducted the inspection being employed by the defendant No.1 for and on behalf of the principal/buyer but, suddenly and mysteriously, he left Bangladesh without informing the plaintiff. At this stage, they also took undue advantage of the sudden demise of Mr Aminul Huq, the former Managing Director of the plaintiff Company. That the plaintiff has strong prima facie case against the fraud of the defendant Nos.1 to 4 and approached the Court with clean hands and the balance of convenience and inconvenience is weighing in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants. The plaintiff will suffer irreparably and the suit will become infructuous if the injunction is not issued restraining the defendant as prayed for and there will be multiplicity of litigations. 

 5. It appears that although the plaintiff alleged about the master letter of credit being a condition precedent for payment under the letters of credit dated 28-9-1999 and 12-10-1999 but nothing could be placed before us to show any condition precedent or that there was a legal condition for prior satisfaction of the amount under the master letter of credit prior to the satisfaction as to payment under the above-mentioned letter of credit for which the Sonali Bank is under a legal obligation to pay of the respondents.
